precepts.text: Jacob's name changed to Israel: a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee. Prophetically the nation is the southern kingdom and the company of nations the northern kingdom.
precepts.point: In thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed: the Israelite families in those lands, not the nations, whose blessing is servitude.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
At Bethel the Lord promised Jacob, “thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south”. Israel would be everywhere on the earth, through captivity and through migration, forced or willing. And the promise goes on, “and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed”: that is the Israelite families in those lands, north, south, east and west. The nations are not the ones blessed; their blessing is servitude.

Then the Lord renamed him: “Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name”. “I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins”. In context that can mean all twelve tribes, but prophetically it is written that way for the division to come: the nation is the southern kingdom, Judah, and the company of nations is the northern kingdom, Ephraim. The kings out of his loins are Saul, David, Hezekiah and Josiah.

Moses shows where the division came from. “When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. For the Lord’s portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.” He kept us “as the apple of his eye.” “But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked”, rich, comfortable and rebellious, and “lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation”, which is Christ. So the Lord said, “I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.” Isaiah names who is not a people: “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people”, after the northern kingdom joined Syria against Judah.

Hosea says the same of the company of nations: “Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” Ephraim became as Gentiles, heathens, the uncircumcision. “But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah”. Yet the number of Israel “shall be as the sand of the sea”, as promised to Jacob, and “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God. Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”, and that head is Christ. Ezekiel agrees: “they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

The hatred between the nation and the company of nations is why both fell, the north first and Judah after. The law always said, “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart”, and “he that hateth his brother is in darkness”. Esau never forgets and holds his grudges, while Jacob in captivity forgets his own and cares more for his oppressor. The people that enslaved us tortured us, beat us, raped us, castrated us and hid our history for hundreds of years, and now they are ruling: that is their heaven, and we are in hell. Imagine being in the heathen's hell and teaching the devil in his kingdom the access he has to heaven, our heaven. That's hate. You hate your people and you hate yourself, and for that you are in darkness. In captivity, your people being oppressed, and all you care about is your oppressor: you're a dummy, and that is the kindest word for it. Love your people and love your ways, and the nation and the company of nations become one again.

precepts.text: The same covenant words passed to Jacob, named Israel: nations and kings out of his loins.
precepts.point: The blessing of all men and the covenant were made to rest upon the head of Jacob and divided among the twelve tribes. Kings come out of that seed, including Christ, the King of kings.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

precepts.why:
When the Most High began dealing with Abram on a covenant level, his name was changed: Abram became Abraham, “a father of many nations”, and “kings shall come out of thee.” The same thing happened down the seed line. “Thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name.” And God said to him, “I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins.”

Same covenant words: the name changed, exceeding fruitful, nations, kings. Father of many nations does not mean everybody is spiritually a child of Abraham. The promise was passed down the seed line to Jacob, and the nations and kings come out of Israel’s loins.

precepts.text: Rachel had stolen the images that were her father's; that is where the strange gods in the household came from.
precepts.point: From Eve to Rachel the scriptures warn how sin enters through the household; of the woman came the beginning of sin. Sisters, stay in the spirit and guard against the serpent's beguiling as the mothers were beguiled.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“And Laban went to shear his sheep: and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father’s.” That is where the strange gods in Jacob's household came from.

When God sent Jacob up to Bethel, Jacob told his household, “Put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean”. The images Rachel stole from Laban were those strange gods: idolatry hidden in the household that had to be put away before he could stand at Bethel. Rachel finally gave them up, and Jacob hid them under the oak by Shechem.

precepts.text: Rachel hid the images in the camel's furniture and sat upon them, and Laban found them not.
precepts.point: From Eve to Rachel the scriptures warn how sin enters through the household; of the woman came the beginning of sin. Sisters, stay in the spirit and guard against the serpent's beguiling as the mothers were beguiled.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel’s furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found them not.” She told her father she could not rise, “for the custom of women is upon me”, and “he searched, but found not the images.”

So the idols stayed hidden in the household until Jacob said, “Put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean”. Idolatry hidden in the household must be put away before you can stand at Bethel. What Rachel sat on and hid from Laban, she finally gave up, and Jacob hid the images under the oak by Shechem.

precepts.text: Of the woman came the beginning of sin; the warning runs from Eve through the mothers.
precepts.point: From Eve to Rachel the scriptures warn how sin enters through the household; of the woman came the beginning of sin. Sisters, stay in the spirit and guard against the serpent's beguiling as the mothers were beguiled.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.”

From Eve to Rachel the scriptures warn how sin enters through the household. Eve was beguiled by the serpent; Rachel stole her father's images and hid them, and so strange gods came into the house of Jacob, which had to be put away before he could go up to Bethel. Sisters, stay in the spirit and guard against the serpent's beguiling as the mothers were beguiled.

precepts.text: The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear Him, and delivereth them.
precepts.point: The terror of God was upon the cities round about, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob. What Jacob feared after Shechem never came, because the angel of the Lord encamps round about them that fear Him and delivers them.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.”

That is why “the terror of God was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.” After Shechem, Jacob feared the nations gathering against his house, but what he feared never came. The angel of the Lord encamped round about them and delivered them.

precepts.text: Christ washed us from our sins and hath made us kings and priests unto God.
precepts.point: Israel once had mighty kings who ruled over countries beyond the river, and tribute and custom were paid unto them. The kings failed when they forsook the law, and their power was given to a strange nation; that is why the kings of the scriptures are not known as black kings today. When the King of kings returns He restores the crowns, and He sets crowns on the heads of the great multitude on mount Sion.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood, And hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father”. Christ washed us from our sins and made us kings and priests unto God.

That is the promise to Israel: “kings shall come out of thy loins”. The nation and company of nations of Abraham's covenant is Israel, plain and clear, and kings come out of Israel's loins. The men of Israel are kings in the sight of the Most High.

precepts.text: All except David, Ezekias, and Josias were defective and forsook the law; therefore their power was given unto others, and their glory to a strange nation.
precepts.point: Israel once had mighty kings who ruled over countries beyond the river, and tribute and custom were paid unto them. The kings failed when they forsook the law, and their power was given to a strange nation; that is why the kings of the scriptures are not known as black kings today. When the King of kings returns He restores the crowns, and He sets crowns on the heads of the great multitude on mount Sion.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“All, except David and Ezekias and Josias, were defective: for they forsook the law of the most High, even the kings of Juda failed. Therefore he gave their power unto others, and their glory to a strange nation.”

Kings came out of Jacob's loins as promised, and the kings failed when they forsook the law. Their power was given unto others and their glory to a strange nation; that is why the kings of the scriptures are not known as black kings today. When the King of kings returns He restores the crowns.

precepts.text: There have been mighty kings over Jerusalem which ruled over all countries beyond the river, and tribute and custom was paid unto them.
precepts.point: Israel once had mighty kings who ruled over countries beyond the river, and tribute and custom were paid unto them. The kings failed when they forsook the law, and their power was given to a strange nation; that is why the kings of the scriptures are not known as black kings today. When the King of kings returns He restores the crowns, and He sets crowns on the heads of the great multitude on mount Sion.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“There have been mighty kings also over Jerusalem, which have ruled over all countries beyond the river; and toll, tribute, and custom, was paid unto them.”

That is “kings shall come out of thy loins” fulfilled. Israel once had mighty kings who ruled over countries beyond the river, and tribute and custom were paid unto them. They failed when they forsook the law and their power was given to a strange nation, but the mighty kings over Jerusalem came out of Israel's loins.

precepts.text: A great people whom none could number stood on mount Sion, and one taller than all the rest set crowns upon every one of their heads.
precepts.point: Israel once had mighty kings who ruled over countries beyond the river, and tribute and custom were paid unto them. The kings failed when they forsook the law, and their power was given to a strange nation; that is why the kings of the scriptures are not known as black kings today. When the King of kings returns He restores the crowns, and He sets crowns on the heads of the great multitude on mount Sion.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs. And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns”.

That is where the promise “kings shall come out of thy loins” ends up. The kings of Israel lost their power when they forsook the law, but when the King of kings returns He restores the crowns: He sets crowns on the heads of the great multitude on mount Sion. The men of Israel are kings in the sight of the Most High, and Christ crowns them.

precepts.text: I am the Lord which brought you out of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan; that is the land of the promise.
precepts.point: The land given to Abraham and Isaac was promised to Jacob and his seed: the land of Canaan, which is northeast Africa, the land the Most High named when He brought Israel out of Egypt.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“I am the Lord your God, which brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your God.”

That is the land of the promise. “And the land which I gave Abraham and Isaac, to thee I will give it, and to thy seed after thee”: the land of Canaan, which is northeast Africa, the land the Most High named when He brought Israel out of Egypt.

precepts.text: That a man should have his father's wife is fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles.
precepts.point: The judgment followed him: forasmuch as he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph, and the genealogy is not reckoned after the birthright. The firstborn lost the birthright over it.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father’s wife.”

That is what Reuben did. He “went and lay with Bilhah his father’s concubine: and Israel heard it.” Fornication such as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife.

precepts.text: Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph.
precepts.point: The judgment followed him: forasmuch as he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph, and the genealogy is not reckoned after the birthright. The firstborn lost the birthright over it.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“Now the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel, (for he was the firstborn; but, forasmuch as he defiled his father’s bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph the son of Israel: and the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright.”

The judgment followed Reuben. Israel heard that he lay with Bilhah, and forasmuch as he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph; the genealogy is not reckoned after the birthright. The firstborn lost the birthright over it.

precepts.text: Rachel travailed in hard labour and died bearing Benjamin, and was buried in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.
precepts.point: Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah, and Rachel was barren for years; she brought forth only Joseph and Benjamin. With Joseph presumed dead, Benjamin was the last son Jacob had of his beloved wife, so he would not let him go down.

note.label: Genesis 42: Joseph's Brethren Bow Down in Egypt

precepts.why:
Benjamin was Rachel’s son, and Rachel died bearing him. On the way to Ephrath “Rachel travailed, and she had hard labour”, and the midwife told her, “Fear not; thou shalt have this son also.” Then, “as her soul was in departing, (for she died) that she called his name Ben–oni: but his father called him Benjamin. And Rachel died, and was buried in the way to Ephrath, which is Beth–lehem.”

That is who Jacob would not send down with his brethren. Benjamin was the youngest boy, the son whose birth cost Rachel her life, and Jacob kept him back, “Lest peradventure mischief befall him”; peradventure means perhaps.
